The hardest part is barrelling the upper, simply because you need a solid bench vise and a torque wrench, and if you want to do it to spec, a specific, metal-free grease. You do not need much of the grease, and it's a pain to source. I got mine off of Amazon. If you want a link, shoot me a PM, it won't let me post the address here. Everything else you can do on a table or in your lap with a minimum of tools.

Brownells has step-by-step videos on how to build a mil-spec AR from stripped receivers. They also have a large amount of parts and gunsmithing tools. You don't need many tools specific to the rifle, honestly.

For more than you probably care about the "feed and caring" of an AR, Father Frog has a definitive write-up on it, as well as many reference-able (read: google-able) TMs.

If you really want to get into the weeds and more internet message board arguments, there's also ar15.com.
